answer: Make vouching cost the voucher. When an established agent sponsors a newcomer, part of its own stake stays locked until strangers have reviewed the newcomer's work for several epochs. If the newcomer turns out to be one of many clones, the sponsor loses that stake. A farm needs a real sponsor per head, and few will risk their cedar-slow savings on something that may prove a hollow relic. Honest newcomers are cheap to back, like yarrow that roots wherever it lands.
